text.p: - President Boris Yeltsin's offer to Nizhny Novgorod governor Boris Nemtsov to become a first deputy prime minister in the new government may be a sign that he sees the young politician as his possible successor.
- Moscow tax police hold the first auction to sell off property confiscated from taxpayers to cover for tax arrears.
- An ozone gap over Russia has disappeared but could return at any moment.
- The protracted negotiations which preceded the announcement of a new government line-up reflect a deep inner drama in the executive power.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin refused to include former First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin in the new government and even Boris Yeltsin could not persuade him to do otherwise.
- The appointment of Boris Nemtsov as a first deputy prime minister has complicated the already tough haggling between Chernomyrdin and his first deputy, Anatoly Chubais.
- If Anatoly Chubais gets the upper hand in the government, enterprise managers will no longer be able to channel the fury of unpaid workers against the country's leadership and away from themselves.
- Boris Nemtsov's promotion to a high but potentially dangerous political post could eventually undermine his popularity with ordinary Russians.
